Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): {Has the story of Moses reached you?} This is a question about a great matter whose occurrence is certain; i.e., has his story reached you? {When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa} — this is the place where Allah spoke to him, bestowed upon him the favour of prophethood, sent him with revelation, and chose him. {34–36} That is, when the Greatest Resurrection (al-Qiyamah al-Kubra) and the Great Terror come, before which every other hardship becomes insignificant, then on that day the parent will be distracted from his child, the companion from his companion, and every lover from his beloved. "The human being will remember what he strove for": in the world, of good and of evil. So he will wish for an increase of even an atom's weight in his good deeds, and he will be grieved and saddened by an increase of even an atom's weight in his evil deeds. He will know then that the basis of his profit and loss is what he strove for in the world, and every means and connection that existed in the world, except for deeds, will be cut off. "And Hell will be made manifest for whoever sees": that is, it will be placed in plain view for everyone, prepared for its people and ready to seize them, awaiting the command of its Lord.

{37–39} "As for he who transgressed": that is, who exceeded the limit by boldly committing grave sins and did not confine himself to what God has set as bounds. "And preferred the life of this world": over the Hereafter, so that his striving and his time became wholly absorbed in its portions and desires, and he forgot the Hereafter and working for it. "Then indeed Hell will be his refuge": that is, his abode and dwelling, for one whose state is this.

{40–41} "But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord": that is, feared standing before Him and being recompensed with justice. This fear affected his heart, so he "restrained the self from" its desire that would turn it away from obedience to God, and his desire came to follow what the Messenger brought. He struggled against desire and lust, which turn one away from good. "Then indeed Paradise": encompassing every good, joy and bliss, "will be his refuge": for one who bears this description.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 79, verse 42–46:

{42 – 44} That is: the obstinate deniers of the Resurrection ask you {about the Hour}: when will it occur? {When is its appointed time?} So Allah answered them with His words: ﴿In what [position] are you to mention it?﴾ That is: what benefit is there for you or for them in mentioning it and knowing the time of its coming? There is no outcome beneath that. For this reason, since the knowledge of the Hour holds no religious or worldly benefit for the servants, but rather the benefit lies in its being hidden from them, He concealed the knowledge of it from all creation and reserved its knowledge for Himself, saying: ﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ That is: its knowledge ends with Him, as He said in another verse: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when is its appointed time? Say: "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time except Him."﴾

{45 – 46} ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ That is: your warning benefits only those who fear the coming of the Hour and dread standing before Allah. They are the ones who are concerned only with preparing for it and working for its sake. As for the one who does not believe in it, he is not to be cared about, nor is his obstinacy, because it is obstinacy founded on denial and stubbornness. When it reaches this state, answering him is futility, from which the Most Wise of judges is far removed.

Finished. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
